models.sample_description: Annual Compustat Annual PST firm-year fits. For each retained formation year t=1984–88, Equation (4) is re-estimated using observations from 1981 through t. independent_variables.name: BC_{t,i}
independent_variables.definition: The year-t bias component of the book-to-market ratio, measured as the firm effect from Equation (4). It represents persistent firm-specific variation in BTM.

evidence.quote: The bias component is measured as the firm effect
BC denotes the firm effect (bias component)

independent_variables.name: LC_{t,i}
independent_variables.definition: The year-t lag component, measured as the projection of BTM from the Equation (4) fitted current and lagged returns while ignoring the fixed effects. It sums the seven return terms (current plus six lags), centered by the corresponding time and firm means with the overall mean added; it represents BTM variation due to unrecognized past market returns.

evidence.quote: The lag component is measured as the projection of the BTM from the estimation of equation (4) ignoring the fixed effects
LC represents the variation in the BTM due to unrecognized past market returns.

COORDINATOR-VERIFIED MATHEMATICAL TRANSCRIPTION (Lag-component centered-return projection, Table3 page prose, physical PDF page 12): LC_(t,i) = sum_(j=0)^6 beta_j * (R_(t-j,i) - R_(t-j,.) - R_(.,i) + R_(.,.)). The source calls R_(t-j,.), R_(.,i), and R_(.,.) the time, firm, and overall means of R_(t-j,i), respectively.

sample_extraction.data_section_full_text:
3.1 SAMPLE 
DATA 
All data are obtained from Compustat's Annual PST tape covering 
1974-93. MV is measured at the end of the fiscal year and NI is measured as annual net income available for common shareholders. Fiscalyear security returns adjusted for stock dividends and splits are denoted 
R. When necessary, time subscripts precede firm subscripts, though both 
are suppressed when feasible. ROEt is defined as NItIBVt-1. To mitigate 
the effects of outliers, BTM is winsorized at 0 and 4, ROE is winsorized at 
-1 and + 1, and R is winsorized at 3. These rules affect approximately 1% 
in each of the corresponding tails of these variables. Descriptive statistics are reported in panels A and B of table 1. The median BTM trends 
downward since 1974, reflecting a rising stock market and perhaps more 
conservative accounting during this period. Median ROE trends upward 
from 1975 to 1979 and downward thereafter, roughly tracking interest 
rates. 
Our reported results reflect the survivorship biases in the Compustat 
Annual PST sample. While we are uncertain how these biases affect our 
results, some insight might be gained from Breen and Korajczyk's [1993] 
finding that the BTM's ability to predict future security returns is approximately halved after controlling for survivorship. Our method of 
estimating the bias and lag components essentially precludes any ability 
to deal with Compustat dropping troubled firms (but not backfilling
